stories.headline: Paga expands Direct Debit access for businesses beyond its network
stories.summary: African fintech Paga has expanded its Direct Debit functionality for businesses using its payments infrastructure platform, Paga Engine. The update allows merchants to collect recurring payments directly from customer bank accounts across other Nigerian financial institutions outside of Paga's internal network.

stories.headline: Flutterwave spent a decade moving money. Now it wants to keep more of it.
stories.summary: African fintech giant Flutterwave is re-evaluating its business model after nearly a decade of facilitating cross-border payments across the continent. Founded in 2016 by Olugbenga Agboola, the company built its core reputation by offering payment infrastructure to global enterprises like Uber, and is now focusing on increasing margins and retaining revenue.

stories.headline: NextDC shares soar nearly 51% after Goodman, Digital Realty stake purchases
stories.summary: Shares of Australian data center operator NextDC surged over 50% after Goodman Group and U.S.-listed Digital Realty moved to acquire up to 9.9% stakes in the company. NextDC's board labeled the move opportunistic, noting it followed recent power supply delays at its M3 Melbourne facility and a revised fiscal 2027 guidance.

stories.headline: CERT-In Flags AI-Driven Cyberattacks On Indian BFSI
stories.summary: India's Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) has issued a critical warning to the banking, financial services, and insurance (BFSI) sector regarding an increase in AI-driven cyberattacks. The advisory alerts financial institutions to sophisticated threats leveraging artificial intelligence for targeted phishing, automated system exploitation, and deepfake impersonation.

stories.headline: Safaricom makes more from M-PESA overdrafts as borrower numbers surge
stories.summary: Safaricom reported KES 4.9 billion ($38 million) in revenue from its M-PESA overdraft service, Fuliza, during its half-year investor briefing in Nairobi. Fuliza's revenue grew 86% as the number of active borrowers nearly doubled to 17.2 million, making mobile lending Safaricom's fastest-growing revenue stream over traditional payments.
